exposure: introduction of additional feeding types at hospital discharge
outcome: breastfeeding success at 6 months postnatal age
cohort: The cohort consisted of 89 discharged very-low-birth-weight (VLBW) infants whose mothers desired breastfeeding.
finding: 55.1% of very-low-birth-weight infants achieved successful breastfeeding at 6 months postnatal age, with inadequate milk supply identified as the main reason for unsuccessful breastfeeding.
mod_finding: Being born via cesarean section was significantly associated with unsuccessful breastfeeding at 6 months postnatal age.
